Steam or GOG? Going to buy TIS-100 and have accounts on gog and steam. Both same price. So a thought experiment. Curious which service should I buy from and why?
Both companies are pretty great. I'd prefer steam since they are heavily supporting Linux nowadays.

GOG all the way. Their games are DRM free, so once you buy it, you own it, and there is no server that can ever shut down that will make it so that you can't play it. The only downside is that you can't compare scores with steam friends ingame, but this is a niche enough game that isn't a huge deal for most I'd expect.

It is awesome though, I'd recommend it highly if you think the premise is interesting. I've bought copies for a couple of my friends now.
I was thinking GOG. Though I've been debating about setting up a SteamOS Machine.

I think it just boils down to ease of use vs control. Steam is easier to use for managing your installed games, but GoG gives you full control over the game and its files. I haven't tried the GoG Galaxy system though. If that's on par with Steam, then GoG might be the way to go.

If something is on both, go GOG.

Pros:

DRM free.

No client needed to play or download.

Download gets you an actual installer that you can transfer to another of your PCs (I'm not condoning illegal shit but) or share with a friend for demo purposes

Valve is more worried about SteamOS and a slightly misguided version of gaming, whereas GOG is owned and operated by the current world champion of giving a damn about their customers.

You own your copy, rather than a license to use a copy that can be revoked at any time for literally any reason at valve/steams discretion.

Cons:

If a game relies on steam for most of it's MP matchmaking, it will be slightly more complex (maybe, usually not the least bit different) making/joining MP games.

Not part of steam system (tear tear)

Um...you have to click a button to update? I dunno, there truly isn't a lot of cons unless you're one hell of a lazy sack of shit.

If it's not a multiplayer game (never heard of it), then GOG for sure.
With GOG you own the software. With Steam you don't.
When I'm buying new games I always check GOG first. DRM free is a big plus in my book.

I always recommend GOG over Steam due to the DRM and ownership aspects many other users talked about. There is, however, 2 other issues that I consider important:

  • If you are a multi-platform player, GOG has no Galaxy client for Linux (Galaxy is like Steam, in the basic sense. It downloads and updates all GOG games). It may bit sound important, but I'd you have more than a few games, it starts being a pain in the arse manually doing it.

  • If you play on more than one computer, there is no "Cloud save" like in Steam. This means that you must manually take care of that.

With that is mind, it's your choice. Be aware that both issues I referred are currently on the works, and should be released soon.
